agent_notes.jorunn: Brand identity complete. Created comprehensive guidelines covering brand positioning ('single source of truth for your tech stack'), tone of voice (3 traits: Direct, Data-driven, Minimal), naming rationale for Stackr, color palette with severity indicators for CVE display, and Inter typography pairing. Key decision: avoid marketing language; let the product's value speak. Tagline: 'One dashboard. Total visibility.' All copy should follow the tone guide's dos/don'ts framework.
agent_notes.bjorn: System architecture complete. Stack: FastAPI + Supabase (Postgres+Auth) + Redis (ARQ) + OSV.dev. Multi-tenancy via row-level security. JWT auth. Async vulnerability scanning via ARQ worker dyno on Railway. Full ERD, C4 context diagram, component diagram, and 3 decision records (auth, multi-tenancy, async jobs) in output/llm-test/architecture/2026-04-11-system-architecture.md. Arve must not bypass RLS with service role key in user-facing routes. Magnus: flag JWT revocation and tenant data confidentiality. Dag: needs web + worker dynos + Redis add-on on Railway.
agent_notes.magnus: Compliance & GDPR review complete. 17 LAUNCH BLOCKER items identified — key ones for arve: API keys must use envelope encryption (never plaintext), passwords must use bcrypt/Argon2id, RBAC enforced server-side only, audit logs must be write-once/append-only, team data isolation enforced at data layer (no cross-tenant leakage), immediate access revocation on member removal. Privacy policy clauses drafted. Data minimisation recommendations for dependency metadata. Full checklist at output/llm-test/compliance/2026-04-11-compliance-checklist.md.
agent_notes.ingrid: UI/UX wireframes complete. Four screens delivered: (1) Dashboard home with stack health snapshot (stat cards, dependency table, scan CTA), (2) Dependency detail view (version history, CVE list with severity badges, team context), (3) Stack settings (GitHub integration, manifest import, manual entry, scan frequency, team management), (4) Onboarding flow (signup, team creation, stack creation, dependency import with GitHub OAuth option). All screens include empty states, error handling, mobile responsiveness, dark mode support, and Tailwind design tokens. Design is clean/minimal per brand, numbers-forward, with 3-click max to core features. Severity badges use color + icon + text (red/amber/orange/blue/green). Polling pattern for async scans (every 3s) aligns with architecture. Handoff artifact ready for Arve's implementation phase.
agent_notes.dag: Infrastructure & CI/CD complete. Deliverables: docker-compose.yml (API + worker + Postgres + Redis + pgAdmin for local dev), multi-stage Dockerfile (builder + slim runtime, non-root user), GitHub Actions CI (ruff + mypy + pytest with real Postgres/Redis service containers), GitHub Actions CD (build + push to GHCR on merge to main). Key constraint enforced: SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY only set on worker service variables on Railway, not web service — matches bjorn's RLS requirement. Railway webhook trigger for CD is documented but requires manual activation (add RAILWAY_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK secret + uncomment job). All files at output/llm-test/infra/. Arve: use output/llm-test/infra/ as the basis for the project repo's infra setup.
agent_notes.arve: Backend API implementation complete. Full FastAPI scaffold at projects/llm-test/backend/. Delivered: 8 SQLAlchemy models matching bjorn's ERD + audit_logs + api_keys; Alembic migration with RLS policies; auth dependency injection (JWT validation via Supabase secret, team context via X-Team-Id header); routers for /auth, /teams, /stacks, /dependencies, /vulnerabilities, /scan-jobs; envelope-encrypted API key service (AES-256-GCM, magnus C1/C2); write-only audit log service (magnus G1/G2); RBAC server-side (magnus E1), immediate revocation on member removal (magnus E3), last-active tracking (magnus E2); ARQ worker integrating OSV.dev querybatch; 28-test pytest suite with in-memory SQLite fixture; pyproject.toml + .env.example. Follow-up needed: account deletion (B1), data export (B2), API key management endpoints before launch.

kickoff_description:
A SaaS product called Stackr — a developer tool that lets teams track their tech stack,
  dependencies, and security vulnerabilities in one dashboard. Needs architecture, a working
  backend API in Python, compliance check, and a brand identity.
